angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 24,729,352 km at 113.25 pc = 2.92 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85693: distance 113.25 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.025), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 113.25 +/- 2.831 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2943 +/- 0.0921 mas (same row, RUWE 2.29), 90.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 35.546 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85693: radius 35.546 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 352.896 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.065) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 24,729,352 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4199 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85693: effective temperature 4199 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.061) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85693: effective temperature 4199 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.061) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam Her: spectral type K3.5III (1989ApJS...71..245K)
luminositySource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4570796456599587200, flags_flame 10: lum_flame 537.05334 solar luminosities (16th to 84th percentiles 526.1248 to 548.20886); its log10 is recorded
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * lam Her: projected rotation speed 17 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (1970CoKwa.189....0U)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 780) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
